title: Register multiplication run
statement: Let $C,e$ be natural numbers, let $m$ and $o$ be Booleans, let $f$ map finite bit strings to finite bit strings, let $h$ be a finite bit string, let $k$ be an element of $	ext{Fin}(e+2)$, let $B$ be a natural number, and let $v$ assign a natural number to each of fourteen registers. Suppose every register value is at most $B$, registers $6$, $10$, and $11$ are $0$, and the product of the values in registers $7$ and $8$ is at most $B$. Then the computation can run from the product-copy state with parameters $o,k$ and register vector $v$ to the power state with parameters $o,k-1$ and register vector obtained by replacing register $7$ with the product of its initial value and register $8$, while the result remains empty and every configuration before the endpoint satisfies the program’s instruction-side conditions and register bound $B$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps finite bit strings to finite bit strings
$v$ assigns natural-number values to fourteen registers
Every register value is at most $B$
The product of registers $7$ and $8$ is at most $B$
replaced:
Let $C,e,B$ be natural numbers, let $m$ and $o$ be Boolean parameters, let $f$ be a
function from bit strings to bit strings, let $h$ be a bit string, let $k<e+2$, and let
$v$ assign a natural number to each of the fourteen registers. Suppose every register
value is at most $B$, registers $6$, $10$, and $11$ are zero, and the product of the
values in registers $7$ and $8$ is at most $B$. In the counter program parameterized by
$C,e,m$, there is a run from state “product copy” with parameters $o,k$ and register
vector $v$ to state “power” with parameters $o,k-1$ and register vector obtained by
replacing register $7$ by the product of its initial value and register $8$; the result
field remains empty, and every configuration before the endpoint satisfies the program's
safety condition and register bound $B$.
